hook_text: Right now, you are zooming through space at about 30 kilometres every second. So why can't you feel it?
clip_script: Sutherland, Northern Cape. Dark skies, giant telescope. The Sun? A star, so big that a million Earths could fit inside. Earth? Planet number three. And we never stop moving, round and round the Sun on a path called an orbit, held by gravity. One lap takes about 365 days: one year. The extra quarter day each year? After four years, it becomes 29 February. Leap year!
visual_style: Whiteboard Sun with a tiny Earth travelling around a dotted orbit and a calendar flipping through the months.
mood: Wonder-filled and starry, then playful about leap-year birthdays.
pacing: Slow and spacious under the stars, then quick for the leap year twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and work out how many laps around the Sun you have made.
